title: Google workers tell their employer not to punish schools that don't want AI
lede: Hundreds of Google employees signed an Alphabet Workers Union petition against a policy that would cut off Search for schools that disable Gemini tools.

points: The policy, announced on Election Day, takes effect next year for schools that turn off Google's AI features.
Protests against it were held in New York and six other US cities.
New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago school districts are discussing alternative search engines.
The petition argues educators should choose how AI enters their curriculum and warns schools may drop Google entirely.
Leadership has acknowledged the letter without answering its demands; one engineer says most staff learned of the policy publicly.

points.text: Some say schools are asking Google to maintain a second, AI-free product; others compare the bundling to Internet Explorer and Windows.
Commenters read the move as an attempt to hook children early, pointing to years of cheap Chromebooks in classrooms.
A parent says their child's school Chromebook shows no AI at all, so the article's picture does not match their district.
Many ask why schools do not simply switch search engines; a reply suggests most school IT departments are thinly staffed.
